title: Falling
scope: Choose the objectives in your school’s topic list. These are original practice questions with illustrative values, not a claim of an official school paper format.

objectives.label: Explain and use free-fall acceleration.
objectives.note: When gravity is the only force, the local acceleration does not depend on the object’s mass.

objectives.label: Explain and use terminal velocity.
objectives.note: A falling object reaches terminal velocity when drag balances weight and its velocity stops changing.

objectives.label: Explain and use mass and lunar weight.
objectives.note: Mass is unchanged by location, while weight depends on the local gravitational field strength.

objectives.label: Explain and use projectile motion.
objectives.note: Ignoring air resistance, horizontal and vertical components of projectile motion can be considered separately.

objectives.label: Explain and use circular motion.
objectives.note: Changing direction at constant speed changes velocity and requires acceleration towards the centre.

cards.definition: When gravity is the only force, the local acceleration does not depend on the object’s mass.
cards.explanation: Use the relationship in the stated conditions and name the objects or system being considered.
cards.example: Why does a falling feather in air not by itself refute equal free-fall acceleration? Air exerts a force that can be significant relative to the feather’s weight. The feather is not in the gravity-only conditions of ideal free fall.
cards.confusion: Equal acceleration does not mean equal gravitational force on different masses.
cards.question: Explain free-fall acceleration from memory. What common mistake must you avoid?
cards.answer: When gravity is the only force, the local acceleration does not depend on the object’s mass. Equal acceleration does not mean equal gravitational force on different masses.

cards.definition: A falling object reaches terminal velocity when drag balances weight and its velocity stops changing.
cards.explanation: Use the relationship in the stated conditions and name the objects or system being considered.
cards.example: A parachute opens while a person falls. Explain why the person initially slows. Opening the parachute greatly increases drag. Drag can exceed weight, producing an upward resultant force while the person moves downwards.
cards.confusion: At terminal velocity the forces are not absent.
cards.question: Explain terminal velocity from memory. What common mistake must you avoid?
cards.answer: A falling object reaches terminal velocity when drag balances weight and its velocity stops changing. At terminal velocity the forces are not absent.

cards.definition: Mass is unchanged by location, while weight depends on the local gravitational field strength.
cards.explanation: Use the relationship in the stated conditions and name the objects or system being considered.
cards.example: An instrument weighs 24 N on the Moon, where g = 1.6 N/kg. Calculate its mass and explain whether this mass changes when it returns to Earth. Mass = weight ÷ gravitational field strength. 24 ÷ 1.6 = 15 kg. Its mass remains 15 kg on Earth; its weight changes with the gravitational field.
cards.confusion: Low lunar weight is not a loss of mass.
cards.question: Explain mass and lunar weight from memory. What common mistake must you avoid?
cards.answer: Mass is unchanged by location, while weight depends on the local gravitational field strength. Low lunar weight is not a loss of mass.

cards.definition: Ignoring air resistance, horizontal and vertical components of projectile motion can be considered separately.
cards.explanation: Use the relationship in the stated conditions and name the objects or system being considered.
cards.example: A ball is projected horizontally in still air with air resistance neglected. Describe its horizontal speed and vertical speed during descent. Its horizontal speed stays constant. Its downward vertical speed increases because gravity accelerates it.
cards.confusion: Horizontal motion does not switch off the downward acceleration.
cards.question: Explain projectile motion from memory. What common mistake must you avoid?
cards.answer: Ignoring air resistance, horizontal and vertical components of projectile motion can be considered separately. Horizontal motion does not switch off the downward acceleration.

cards.definition: Changing direction at constant speed changes velocity and requires acceleration towards the centre.
cards.explanation: Use the relationship in the stated conditions and name the objects or system being considered.
cards.example: A ball’s string breaks during horizontal circular motion. Ignore other horizontal forces. State its immediate horizontal path. Explain your answer. It moves along the tangent at the release point. It continues in its instantaneous direction without the inward string force.
cards.confusion: An inward resultant is a role played by real forces, not an additional interaction.
cards.question: Explain circular motion from memory. What common mistake must you avoid?
cards.answer: Changing direction at constant speed changes velocity and requires acceleration towards the centre. An inward resultant is a role played by real forces, not an additional interaction.
